transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I came in today because I just feel wound up almost all day. It's hard to explain, but it feels like my body is constantly bracing for something. Even when I'm just sitting at my computer for work, or trying to relax after dinner, I just have this tension that I can't seem to turn off.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot or feeling anxious about things, even when there's no clear reason for it?

Yes, I do. It seems like my mind just keeps going from one concern to another. I'll be thinking about my sister in Arecibo, or... whether I missed something at the office. And then it shifts to worrying about my husband driving home, or my church commitments, or the bills. I just find myself constantly preparing for problems that haven’t even happened yet.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms along with this constant worrying, such as restlessness, feeling fatigued, muscle tension, or trouble sleeping?

Yes, definitely the trouble sleeping. Most nights I do fall asleep eventually, but... I wake up around three or four in the morning. I'll just be lying there thinking about my sister’s next appointment, or maybe some server issue at work. And even when I technically get enough hours of sleep, I start the morning feeling like I never really rested at all.
Do you feel that your worrying is something you can't control or stop, even when you try?

Yes, it really feels like I can't stop it. I do try. I’ll tell myself, ‘Daniela, enough, just focus on this report,’ but... it doesn't really work. One small thought just turns into five more, and before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour checking my messages or just replaying everything that could go wrong.
Are these worries and physical symptoms, like trouble sleeping and tension, causing you a lot of distress or making it hard to do your usual daily activities, like work or being with family?

Well, I'm still getting everything done. I show up for work, I'm there for my family, and I keep my church commitments. But... it is harder. It takes me longer to finish my reports at work because I'm double-checking everything way more than I used to. And I guess the lack of sleep makes me a bit edgy, because I've had to apologize lately for sounding short with my husband and some of the people I care about. So it doesn't stop me from doing things, but it definitely makes everything feel like more of a struggle.
Do you find that your worrying isn’t just about one specific thing, but rather that your anxiety shifts from one concern to another throughout the day?

Yes, that's exactly it. It's never just one thing. My mind just keeps going from one concern to another all day. I'll be worrying about my sister in Arecibo, and then it shifts to whether I missed something at the office, or if my husband is okay driving home. Then it's on to my church commitments, or the bills... I just find myself constantly preparing for problems that haven't even happened yet.
